candidates.entry: At market close, compute 60-day total return for each ETF in ['DBC','GSG','DBA','USO','UNG','PDBC']; rank them descending. Open long positions in the top 2 ETFs and short positions in the bottom 2 ETFs. Positions are entered at the next day open.
candidates.exit: Close each position at the next day open when either (a) the ETF drops out of its respective top-2/bottom-2 rank, or (b) 30 calendar days have elapsed since entry, whichever comes first.
candidates.sizing: Allocate equal dollar amount to each leg; then scale the entire portfolio to target 8% annualized volatility using the 30-day rolling realized volatility of the portfolio (risk-parity scaling).
candidates.regime_filter: Skip all trades on days when the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) > 25 or when the NBER recession flag is active (US recession).
candidates.rationale: Menkhoff et al. show momentum generates strong excess returns in commodity markets; applying a cross-sectional momentum filter to a diversified basket of commodity ETFs should capture similar returns while volatility-targeting improves risk-adjusted performance.

candidates.entry: For each ETF, compute the 30-day simple moving average (SMA30). Go long an ETF when its price is at least 1% below SMA30 (indicating potential positive roll-yield carry) and go short when its price is at least 1% above SMA30. Enter positions at next day open.
candidates.exit: Close the position at next day open when the price crosses back within ±0.5% of SMA30 or after 45 calendar days, whichever occurs first.
candidates.sizing: Equal dollar allocation per leg; apply risk-parity scaling to achieve a portfolio-wide target volatility of 10% annualized, using a 30-day rolling realized volatility estimate.
candidates.regime_filter: Only trade during periods identified as economic expansions (NBER recession flag = false). Skip all days in recessions.
candidates.rationale: Bakshi et al. find carry strategies outperform in expansionary regimes; using a simple price-vs-SMA proxy for roll yield captures this effect in liquid commodity ETFs.

candidates.entry: Determine macro regime daily: if NBER recession flag = false (expansion) use the momentum rule from futures_momentum_v1; if recession flag = true use the carry rule from futures_carry_v1. Enter positions at next day open accordingly.
candidates.exit: Apply the respective exit rule of the active sub-strategy (30-day rank change or 45-day SMA cross).
candidates.sizing: Risk-parity across all active legs targeting 9% annualized volatility, using a 30-day rolling realized volatility estimate.
candidates.regime_filter: None beyond the regime definition; the strategy is inactive only when both expansion and recession flags are ambiguous (e.g., transition days).
candidates.rationale: Combining the regime-dependent insights of Bakshi et al. with the proven momentum edge from Menkhoff et al. should exploit the dominant driver (momentum or carry) in each macro environment, improving overall Sharpe while keeping drawdowns modest.

candidates.entry: Compute 60-day total return for each ETF; go long the top 2 and short the bottom 2 ETFs. Positions are entered at next day open.
candidates.exit: Close each leg at next day open when the ETF exits its top-2/bottom-2 rank or after 20 calendar days, whichever occurs first.
candidates.sizing: Scale each leg so that the portfolio's 30-day rolling realized volatility equals a target of 10% annualized (volatility-targeting as in Harvey et al.).
candidates.regime_filter: Skip trading on days when VIX > 30.
candidates.rationale: Harvey et al. demonstrate that volatility-targeting materially boosts risk-adjusted returns for commodity strategies; applying it to a momentum-based cross-sectional trade should meet Tier-2 performance thresholds.

candidates.entry: Form two pairs: (USO vs UNG) and (DBC vs GSG). For each pair, compute 30-day momentum for both ETFs; go long the ETF with higher momentum and short the other. Enter at next day open.
candidates.exit: Close the pair when the momentum difference reverses sign or after 40 calendar days, whichever occurs first.
candidates.sizing: Allocate equal risk to each pair; within each pair, size long and short legs equally. Apply portfolio-wide risk-parity scaling to target 9% annualized volatility (30-day rolling vol).
candidates.regime_filter: Skip trading on days when weekly change in US crude oil inventories exceeds 5 million barrels (proxy for market noise) or when VIX > 25.
candidates.rationale: Cross-commodity pair trades capture relative strength, a core finding of Menkhoff et al.; adding a macro filter on oil inventory volatility aligns with Bakshi et al.'s regime considerations, aiming for a robust edge.

notes_to_p3: Backtest each candidate on daily yfinance data (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31). Use rolling 30-day volatility for scaling, NBER recession dates for regime flags, and VIX from ^VIX ticker for regime filters. Verify trade counts exceed 100 total, PF ≥ 1.5, WR ≥ 50%, MDD < 20%.
